result.title: Schedule-Calibrated Commitment Order in Blockwise Masked Diffusion Language Models
result.comment: 9 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Includes appendices and ancillary code for algebraic verification
result.summary: Sequential block schedules can make token commitment in masked diffusion language models appear strongly left-to-right even when within-block order is random or reversed. For equal contiguous blocks processed without interleaving in positional order, with untied irreversible commitments, we use a Spearman-rank identity to express global position-commitment correlation as a deterministic schedule reference plus a weighted mean within-block correlation. In a reported paired study of LLaDA-8B-Instruct on 500 math and code prompts with 256 generated positions and updates, increasing block size from 64 to 128 lowers mean global correlation from 0.9845 to 0.9149. Uniform-random within-block references are already 0.9375 and 0.7500. After calibration, mean within-block correlations are 0.751 and 0.660, so the larger raw residual at block size 128 does not indicate stronger local positional ordering. We give sharp bounds and derive calibrated intervals from reported summaries, while documenting the limitations of the aggregate-only empirical release. The analysis supports schedule-aware interpretation of commitment order; its empirical scope is one checkpoint and two schedules, without evaluation of output quality or inference speed.

AI.brief_summary: 该文用 Spearman 秩恒等式把 masked diffusion 语言模型的全局位置—提交相关性分解为调度参考项与块内相关性的加权和，并对 LLaDA-8B 在两种块大小下的结果做校准，指出较大的原始残差并不代表更强的局部顺序。
AI.relevance_reason: 其调度校准的提交顺序诊断可供核查 diffusion/parallel 生成中“从左到右”是否只是块调度假象，从而可能帮助分析 VLM 并行或扩散式推理状态更新与计算顺序；但材料仅涉及纯文本模型，尚无视觉或 latent reasoning 证据。
